usageNotes: Sends a clean ACPI shutdown signal to a running LXC container and returns a task UPID for async tracking; the container must be in a running state on the specified node. Use `forceStop: true` to guarantee the container stops if the guest does not respond within the timeout window — omitting it on an unresponsive container will leave it running after the timeout expires. Requires the `VM.PowerMgmt` privilege on `/vms/{vmid}`.

examples.summary: Graceful shutdown of container 101 with a 90-second timeout and forced stop fallback

destructiveReason: Stops the container, interrupting all running processes and making its services unavailable until it is started again.
tips: Poll the returned UPID via GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to confirm the shutdown completed before taking dependent actions.
The default timeout of 60 seconds is often too short for containers running databases or heavy workloads — increase it when services need a graceful drain.
Prefer this endpoint over the stop endpoint for production containers; stop is a hard kill, whereas shutdown allows the init system to run teardown hooks.
If the container is already stopped, the API returns an error — check status first with GET /nodes/{node}/lxc/{vmid}/status/current.
